pointers.sentence: A form, a bound field, a list of errors and a widget each draw themselves by handing a template's name and a context to a renderer, an object of `django/forms/renderers.py` that finds the template and renders it.
`get_default_renderer` makes the one the setting `FORM_RENDERER` names, and the built-in templates under `django/forms/templates/` nest, the form's calling each field's.

`RenderableMixin.render`, called with no arguments, renders the object's `template_name` with the dictionary of its `get_context` through the object's own renderer, and marks the result safe; any of the three can be given instead (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableMixin.render`).

A widget has a method of its own, `Widget.render`, which hands its context to the renderer it is given, or to the default one ([Widgets: `Widget` and its subclasses](widgets.md)) (`django/forms/widgets.py:Widget._render`).
`RenderableFormMixin` adds `as_div`, `as_p`, `as_table` and `as_ul`, each rendering a name the class holds, such as `BaseForm.template_name_div` (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableFormMixin`).
`str(form)` renders `BaseForm.template_name`, a property that reads the renderer's form template (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.template_name`).

`BaseForm.__init__` settles a form's renderer once: the argument; else the class's `BaseForm.default_renderer`, made an instance if it is a class; else what `get_default_renderer` returns (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.__init__`).
Its bound fields, error lists and labels use it, and the bound field hands it to the widget (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.as_widget`).

The function is cached, so everything that falls back on it shares one renderer and one engine; under `DjangoTemplates` that engine's loader is the cached one, which keeps each template it has compiled (`django/forms/renderers.py:get_default_renderer`, `django/template/engine.py:Engine.__init__`).

`django/forms/renderers.py:BaseRenderer` holds the names of the default templates, `BaseRenderer.form_template_name`, `BaseRenderer.formset_template_name` and `BaseRenderer.field_template_name`, and `BaseRenderer.bound_field_class`, the form's last resort for its class of bound field.

`BaseRenderer.render` renders the template with the context and an optional request and strips white space from both ends (`django/forms/renderers.py:BaseRenderer.render`); the blank lines inside a piece stay.

No caller in the forms library passes a request, so the backend renders with a plain context and no context processor runs for a form's templates under Django's renderers ([The context: `Context`, `RequestContext` and context processors](../templates/context.md)) (`django/template/context.py:make_context`, `django/template/backends/jinja2.py:Template.render`).

The renderers `DjangoTemplates` and `Jinja2` share `EngineMixin`, whose `EngineMixin.engine` is made on first use and kept on the renderer: an instance of the renderer's template backend, named `"djangoforms"`, with empty `"OPTIONS"`, `"APP_DIRS"` true, and in `"DIRS"` the directory beside `renderers.py` named after the backend's `app_dirname`: `django/forms/templates/`, or `django/forms/jinja2/`, templates of the same names in Jinja2's syntax (`django/forms/renderers.py:EngineMixin.engine`).

Both backends search `"DIRS"` before the applications' directories (`django/template/engine.py:Engine.__init__`, `django/template/backends/base.py:BaseEngine.template_dirs`).

`django/forms/renderers.py:TemplatesSetting` keeps no engine: it finds a template with `django.template.loader.get_template`, which asks each backend of `TEMPLATES` in turn (`django/forms/renderers.py:TemplatesSetting.get_template`, `django/template/loader.py:get_template`).

`BaseForm.get_context` gives the form's template four keys (`django/forms/forms.py:BaseForm.get_context`): `"form"`; `"fields"`, a pair for each visible field of its bound field and its errors; `"hidden_fields"`, the bound fields with hidden widgets; and `"errors"`, a copy of `BaseForm.non_field_errors` with each hidden field's errors added, in a run as `"(Hidden field token) This field is required."`.

`"django/forms/div.html"` prints the form's errors, then a `<div>` for each visible field holding the field's group, and the hidden fields inside the last, if there is one (`django/forms/templates/django/forms/div.html`).
The field's template is its own, if it was given one, or the renderer's (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.template_name`).
The label is `BaseForm.template_name_label`, rendered by `BoundField.label_tag` through the form (`django/forms/boundfield.py:BoundField.label_tag`).

`django/forms/utils.py:flatatt` does the same in Python, for a media asset's attributes among others, but sorts the names, puts the bare ones last and leaves out `None`, which a widget given `{"placeholder": None}` drew, in a run, as `placeholder="None"`.
